summary: Backend-only testing of the new Google OAuth 2.0 Authorization-Code flow (/api/auth/google/start, /api/auth/google/callback), /api/auth/config exposure, CSRF state handling, client-secret leak audit, DB indexes, plus regression on existing auth + financial endpoints. New suite: 25/25 passing. Existing suites test_auth_phase2.py + test_finaura_regression.py: 33 passed / 5 skipped after updating 2 stale assertions that still expected Google to be unconfigured. No client secret leak found in any response body/header/cookie or in supervisor logs (grep 'GOCSPX' => 0 hits). One security hardening issue found: `next` query param allows protocol-relative values (//evil.com) which survive to the frontend redirect => potential open redirect.

minor.issue: OPEN REDIRECT RISK: _frontend_redirect only checks next.startswith('/'), so '//evil.com' passes and is echoed back as ?next=//evil.com to /auth/google/success. GoogleCallback.jsx then calls navigate(next) after a successful sign-in; browsers resolve '//evil.com' as a protocol-relative absolute URL, navigating the freshly-authenticated user off-site. Fix: reject next values starting with '//' or containing ':' / '\\' (e.g. `if not next.startswith('/') or next.startswith('//')`), and/or allow-list known app paths.

Cookie state check is only enforced when the cookie is present (`if cookie_state and cookie_state != state`). An attacker who strips/never sends fin_g_state bypasses the defense-in-depth layer. Server-side single-use state still protects the flow, so severity is low, but consider requiring the cookie when it was set.

Existing-account linking falls back to `db.users.find_one({'email': email})` without requiring claims.email_verified. If Google ever returns an unverified email (possible for some Workspace/3rd-party-IdP setups) this would allow taking over an existing password account. Recommend linking by email only when email_verified is true.
picture/name are only written when the field is absent (`if picture and not user.get('picture')`), so a changed Google avatar never refreshes on subsequent sign-ins. Minor UX/data-freshness issue.
Unconsumed states accumulate until the TTL monitor sweeps (24 rows present during testing). Expected with expireAfterSeconds=0 (Mongo sweeps once per minute after expires_at) — informational only.

Pre-existing (not from this change) tracebacks: 'ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant'. Not reproducible in this run (/api/financial/overview returned 200), but indicates an inf/NaN can still be produced by a computed financial metric for some data shapes.

verified_pass: GET /api/auth/config -> google_enabled=true, google_authcode_enabled=true, google_client_id matches .env and ends with .apps.googleusercontent.com; no 'secret' key and no GOCSPX substring anywhere in body/headers

GET /api/auth/google/start -> 302 to https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with client_id, redirect_uri == GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI (ends /api/auth/google/callback), response_type=code, scope exactly {openid,email,profile}, random 43-char state; 3 consecutive calls produce 3 distinct states
Set-Cookie fin_g_state == state with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/api/auth; Max-Age=600
oauth_states doc persisted with provider=google, next preserved, expires_at exactly 10.00 minutes out; indexes = state_1 (unique) + expires_at_1 (expireAfterSeconds=0)

callback with valid state + bogus code -> #error=token_exchange_failed; no access_token in fragment; no client secret and no raw Google detail (e.g. 'invalid_grant') in the Location header; backend logs only 'Google token exchange failed: 400'
State single-use: second callback with the same state -> #error=invalid_state
next param round-trips through the DB: start?next=/goals -> callback Location contains ?next=/goals
No 5xx from callback for any malformed param combination tested
grep -c GOCSPX on backend.err.log and backend.out.log = 0
Regression: POST /api/auth/register (new email) -> 200 with bearer access_token + user (includes picture, no _id); DELETE /api/auth/account cleanup 200
Regression: POST /api/auth/google (legacy ID-token) with fake credential -> 401 'Invalid Google credential.'
Regression: GET /api/auth/me -> 200 with 'picture' field present; unauthenticated -> 401
Regression: GET /api/financial/overview -> 200 with goals list; POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/goals CRUD verified with read-back persistence
action_items: Harden the `next` parameter against protocol-relative open redirect ('//host') in _frontend_redirect (and optionally validate at /google/start before storing).
Only link a Google identity to an existing email account when claims.email_verified is true.
Optional: refresh name/picture from Google on each sign-in instead of only when absent.
Optional: enforce the fin_g_state cookie match strictly rather than only when the cookie is present.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py _frontend_redirect: `safe_next = next_path if next_path.startswith('/')` is insufficient — '//evil.com' passes; the frontend's navigate(next) then leaves the app. Reject '//' and backslash-prefixed values.
auth.py is 667 lines and mixes email/password, Google (2 flows), Apple, PIN, reset and onboarding. Consider splitting into auth/oauth_google.py, auth/pin.py etc. before it exceeds 700 lines.
Good: client_secret is read from env inside the handler and only ever posted to oauth2.googleapis.com; failures log status code only. Confirmed no leak.

GET /api/goals does not exist (405) — goals are only returned inside /api/financial/overview. Intentional per current design, but worth documenting in test_credentials.md as the endpoint list there is misleading.

The happy path (real Google account -> #access_token in fragment -> GoogleCallback.jsx applyExternalSession) is still UNVERIFIED end-to-end. Known open item: protocol-relative `next` open-redirect. test_auth_phase2.py assertions were updated because Google is now configured in this env.
rca_of_the_issue: Open redirect: /api/auth/google/start stores the raw `next` value (truncated to 200 chars) and _frontend_redirect only validates `startswith('/')`. '//evil.com' satisfies that check, is echoed as ?next=//evil.com, and GoogleCallback.jsx calls navigate(next) after a successful session, which the browser resolves as a protocol-relative external URL. Reproduce: GET /api/auth/google/start?next=//evil.com then complete/observe the callback Location header.
